newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Fourteen Indonesian riot suspects sent to court.
newsitem.headline: Fourteen Indonesian riot suspects sent to court.

text.p: Fourteen Indonesians suspected of involvement in recent riots in central Java have been sent to court on charges of damaging property and disrupting public order, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Sunday.
The paper quoted a police sergeant from Pekalongan police precinct as saying the 14 people were taken to court while 15 other suspects would be sent to court soon.
Police in Pekalongan, a coastal town 300 km (190 miles) east of Jakarta, were not available for comment on Sunday.

At least 60 shops were either burned or ransacked, two cars were set ablaze and a state-run bank was damaged during Wednesday's violence in which the rioters mainly attacked the property of ethnic Chinese.
The paper, which gave no further details on the trial, said originally 31 people were arrested after the riots but two were released due to lack of evidence.
It quoted the police sergeant as saying authorities were looking for five other people suspected of inciting the riots.

Eight people were injured during the incident, apparently sparked by reports that a popular singer, who used to be a supporter of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP), had switched allegiance to the ruling Golkar party.
Pekalongan was the only city in central Java where Golkar lost to the PPP in general elections in 1992.
The country's next general elections will be held on May 29. The only three parties permitted to contest the poll are Golkar, the PPP and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).

Pekalongan's riot was the first violent disturbance in Java since a mob attacked Chinese homes and businesses, Christian churches and Buddhist temples in Tasikmalaya town in western Java in January. Four people died in those riots, set off by an incident of police brutality against a Moslem teacher.
Ethnic clashes between local Dayaks and immigrant Madurese also rocked West Kalimantan province on Borneo island last month. At least 12 people died, military officials and residents said.
